memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: That is why the Book of the Wars of the LORD says: ". . . Zahab in Suphah and the ravines, the Arnon and the slopes of the ravines that lead to the settlement of Ar and lie along the border of Moab." - Num 21:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here Scripture quotes from an ancient record called the Book of the Wars of the Lord. We no longer have this book, but its mention tells us something important. God's people kept memory of the ways the Lord had fought for them.

The very title is striking. These were not merely Israel's wars but the wars of the Lord. Behind every deliverance stood the God who was working out His purposes. The people understood that their survival was not owed to their own strength but to His mighty hand.

There is wisdom in keeping a record of God's faithfulness. When we write down or recount the ways God has helped us, we build a store of memory that steadies us in hard times. Forgetfulness breeds fear, but remembrance breeds faith.

What would your own "book of the wars of the Lord" contain? Perhaps a healing, a provision that came just in time, a door that opened when every other closed. These are not coincidences but the fingerprints of a faithful God. And every battle He has fought points forward to the greatest victory of all, won by Christ over sin and death at the cross (1 Cor 15:57).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What victories has God won in your life that you should remember?
2. Do you keep any record of God's faithfulness?
3. How might remembering God's past help you strengthen your faith today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to remember the battles You have fought for me. Build in me a heart of remembrance that trusts You for the battles still ahead. Amen.
